datasets.title: Datasets
datasets.intro: Each upload becomes a dataset. Cleaning it creates a new version and keeps the original.
datasets.emptyBody: Upload a CSV or Excel file of your sales or orders. We'll check its health and suggest fixes before any analysis.

upload.title: Upload data
upload.intro: Upload one file per dataset. Your original file is always kept.
upload.dropTitle: Drag a file here, or choose one
upload.dropHint: CSV, TSV or Excel (.xlsx), up to {limit} MB. The first row should hold the column names.
upload.name: Dataset name
upload.nameHint: Shown in your dataset list. You can use the file name.
upload.wrong_type: "{file}" isn't a CSV, TSV or .xlsx file. Excel's older .xls format isn't supported; save it as .xlsx first.
upload.empty: "{file}" is empty. Choose a file that has a header row and data.
upload.too_large: "{file}" is {size}, over the {limit} MB limit. Split it or remove unused columns.

detail.processingBody: We're converting the file and detecting column types. Large files take a minute.
detail.checkingBody: Measuring missing values, duplicates and formats in every column.
detail.failedHelp: Check that the file opens in a spreadsheet app and has one header row, then upload it again.

health.relative: Compare scores between versions; the number isn't an absolute grade.
health.noIssues: No problems found. This data is ready for analysis.

plan.intro: Fixes create a new version; your current version stays unchanged. Recommended fixes are selected for you. Review the others before selecting them.
plan.introNoneRecommended: Fixes create a new version; your current version stays unchanged. None of these is recommended automatically for this file, so nothing is selected. Review each one and choose what you want.
plan.none: Nothing to fix. This version needs no cleaning.

riskHelp.low: Changes formatting only; values keep their meaning.
riskHelp.medium: Changes or removes some values. Check before applying.
riskHelp.high: Can change the meaning of your data. Apply only if you're sure.

plan.dateOrderHelp: Both readings are possible in this column. Choose the one your system uses.

plan.applied: Fixes applied. Version {version} is being prepared.

columns.intro: Roles tell the analysis what each column means. Change any that look wrong.
columns.personalHelp: Treated as personal data: the assistant cannot read these values unless your company allows it.
columns.rolesChangedBody: Your current results still use the old roles. Run the analysis again to update them.

preview.caption: First {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} of {total}

range.label: Dates

noData.body: Upload a sales file. Once it is checked and analysed, the figures appear here.

needs.kpis: It needs a revenue column, or quantity and price.
needs.trend_seasonality: It needs a date column and revenue covering at least a few months.
needs.pareto: It needs revenue and a product, category or region column.
needs.cohort_retention: It needs a customer id, a date and several months of orders.
needs.forecast: It needs a date column and at least two years of revenue to learn the seasons.
needs.anomalies: It needs a date column and a few months of daily sales.
needs.segmentation: It needs a customer id, a date and revenue for enough customers.
needs.churn: It needs a customer id, order dates and enough repeat buyers over a year or more.
needs.drivers: It needs revenue plus columns that could explain it, such as price, discount or category.

forecast.title: Forecast
forecast.description: What revenue is likely to be next, as a range, and how well the model did on past data.
forecast.loadFailed: The forecast could not be loaded
forecast.none: No forecast was stored for this analysis.
forecast.takeaway: History on the left, the next {periods} {unit}s on the right. Wider bands mean less certainty.
forecast.aria: Line chart of net revenue history and forecast with 80% and 95% ranges

backtest.title: How well it did on past data
backtest.better: Tested on {windows} past stretches of {horizon} {unit}s, the errors of {model} were {pct}% smaller than simply repeating last season.
backtest.notBetter: Tested on {windows} past stretches of {horizon} {unit}s, {model} was not clearly better than simply repeating last season.
backtest.coverage: The 80% range contained the real value in {pct} of the tested periods.
backtest.lowConfidence: Treat this forecast as a rough guide: it did not beat the simple baseline.
backtest.maseHelp: MASE below 1 means the model beats the seasonal baseline; lower is better.

segments.title: Customer segments
segments.description: Customers grouped by how recently, how often and how much they buy, with a suggested action per group.
segments.loadFailed: The segments could not be loaded
segments.answer: {segment} bring {share}% of revenue from {customers} customers ({pct}% of all customers).
segments.pseudonyms: Customer ids are personal data, so they are shown as pseudonyms.

grid.title: Recency by frequency
grid.takeaway: Each cell counts customers by how recently (rows) and how often (columns) they buy. The top right holds the best customers.
grid.caption: Customers by recency score and frequency score

churn.title: Churn risk
churn.description: Customers who may stop buying, the revenue at stake, and the reasons behind each estimate.
churn.loadFailed: The churn results could not be loaded
churn.yearlySpendHelp: Revenue at stake if they all stopped
churn.expectedLossHelp: Each customer's risk times their spend
churn.modelCheck: Model check: AUC {auc}% on later data
churn.estimateNote: These are estimates from past buying patterns, not certainties.
churn.tableHelp: Sorted by expected loss. Choose a customer to see why.

drivers.title: What drives the risk overall
drivers.unit: Share of the explanation of the model (mean absolute SHAP)

panel.description: The three things that moved this estimate the most.
panel.help: Bar length shows how strongly each reason moved the estimate.
panel.note: An association in past data, not a proven cause.

whatIf.title: What-if
whatIf.description: Estimate what a change to price, discount, volume or cost would do to yearly revenue and profit.
whatIf.limit: Up to {n} scenarios, each between −{max}% and +{max}%.
whatIf.needTarget: Choose a category or product for each scenario that needs one.
whatIf.failed: The estimate could not be made
whatIf.notEnough: Not enough evidence in the data to estimate this change. Try a wider scope or a smaller change.
whatIf.outOfRange: This change goes beyond the prices seen in your data, so the estimate is an extrapolation and may be off.
